story.head: McMichael meets his old team
paras: The Capitals (11-12-0) lost 3-2 to Florida last night, while the Blues (14-9-3) beat Dallas 5-3 the same night. Going in, the Caps are sixth in the Metropolitan (tied for 27th in the NHL) and the Blues sixth in the Central (tied for 14th).

The Capitals have played better than their record (.478) says: their chances are worth about .578, and losses in one-goal games have held them back. The Blues’ record (.596) is about what their chances are worth.

The Blues (1st) and the Capitals (2nd) both take a lot of high-quality shots. The Capitals get their shots through to the net (5th), but give up a lot of dangerous shots (28th). Washington has allowed 3.87 goals a game, the second most in the league. On the other side, the Blues keep things calm after the whistle (lowest) and ice the puck less than almost anyone (2nd). The Capitals’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Blues, and the Capitals are likely to get in the way of a lot of the Blues’ shots.

Alex Tuch (15 G / 5 A / 20 P in 23 GP) is tied for the Capitals’ scoring lead, with seven points in his last five games. Ryan Leonard (10 G / 10 A / 20 P in 23 GP) shares it. For the Blues, Robert Thomas (6 G / 22 A / 28 P in 26 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eleven points in his last five games. Dylan Holloway (9 G / 13 A / 22 P in 26 GP) has a team-high nine goals, with seven points in his last five games.

Charlie Lindgren (3-5-0 / .848 SV% in 6 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Washington, but will likely start. Jordan Binnington (3-3-1 / .845 SV% in 7 GS) has struggled for St. Louis so far, but will likely start.
At home, Jim Montgomery likes to send Toropchenko, Suter and Dvorský out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Ovechkin, Strome and Beauvillier.
